selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the comparison, who does the ruler stand for?
questions.answer: The ruler stands for Allah, our Sustainer and Creator.

questions.question: What kind of people are shown by the servant who does his duty well?
questions.answer: People who perform the daily prayers with eagerness and care.

questions.question: What does the royal land represent?
questions.answer: It represents Paradise.

questions.question: Why is the grave called a station in the comparison?
questions.answer: Because it is a stopping place on the way to the next stage, not the final end.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do people travel that journey at different speeds?
questions.answer: Because their actions are different, and their level of fear of Allah is different.

questions.question: What is the small daily action that prepares a person for the big journey?
questions.answer: Performing the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: Why is it a serious loss to spend almost all day only on worldly life?
questions.answer: Because this world passes quickly, while the hereafter is much longer and more important.

questions.question: What comparison is made with money and chance?
questions.answer: The passage compares neglecting prayer to acting foolishly with money by favoring a poor chance over a much surer and better gain.

questions.question: How does the passage describe prayer for the body?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not hard for the body.

questions.question: How can one hour of worship affect the rest of the day?
questions.answer: With a good intention, it can help the rest of a person’s lawful actions gain worship value too.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It speaks to people who do not pray and also to the speaker’s own self that resists prayer.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the value of one hour used well?
questions.answer: One hour used for prayer can help a person gain great benefit for the hereafter.

questions.question: Why is one day pictured as twenty-four coins?
questions.answer: To show that each hour is like a valuable part of our life that should be used wisely.

questions.question: Why is the hereafter called long life in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it continues beyond this short world.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention very fast travel over huge distances?
questions.answer: To show that righteous people can pass that journey with great ease and speed by Allah’s permission.

questions.question: What percentage of certainty is given for the eternal treasure in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as ninety-nine out of a hundred.

questions.question: Why is skipping prayer called unfair to oneself?
questions.answer: Because a person harms his own future by refusing something small that brings a huge reward.

questions.question: What is needed for normal actions to count as worship?
questions.answer: A correct and sincere intention.

questions.question: How can regular prayer change ordinary daily activities?
questions.answer: It can turn them into worship if the person has a good intention.

questions.question: How can a person make his temporary life lasting in one way?
questions.answer: By praying and having the right intention, so the deeds of this short life bring reward for the hereafter.

questions.question: Match each part of the comparison to its meaning: ruler, twenty-four coins, station, ticket.
questions.answer: Ruler means Allah; twenty-four coins mean the hours of one day; station means the grave; ticket means the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk to the speaker’s own nafs as well as other people?
questions.answer: To show that the struggle against laziness in prayer is personal and real.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect daily time with wealth?
questions.answer: To help us understand that time is precious and should not be wasted.

questions.question: According to the passage, do all people experience the next journey in the same way?
questions.answer: No. Their experience differs based on their deeds and their fear of Allah.
